model_organism.citation: Mice null for NEDD9 (HEF1α) display extensive hippocampal dendritic spine loss and cognitive impairment (PMID: 26683084)
phenotypes: Deficits in learning and memory recall in the Morris water maze
Extensive loss of dendritic spine density in the dentate gyrus and CA1
Spine loss across all branch orders and dendrite regions
Age-dependent spine loss (1.5, 6 and 10 months)
No change in gross hippocampal morphology
No evidence of altered neurogenesis (BrdU stereology)

model_organism.citation: The scaffold protein NEDD9 is necessary for leukemia-cell migration and disease progression in a mouse model of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (PMID: 35523865)
phenotypes: Delayed CLL development
Markedly reduced disease burden
Significant survival benefit
Impaired CLL cell homing, chemotaxis, migration and adhesion

model_organism.citation: Nedd9 Restrains Autophagy to Limit Growth of Early Stage Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (PMID: 34006524)
model_organism.knockout_type: full knockout (Nedd9 deletion in the KP lung cancer model)
phenotypes: Larger tumors with accelerated growth and elevated proliferation in KPN versus KP mice
Cell-autonomous effect shown by orthotopic transplantation
Reduced SRC and AKT activation
Increased active LKB1/AMPK and increased autophagy
Growth advantage eliminated by chloroquine

model_organism.citation: A requirement for Nedd9 in luminal progenitor cells prior to mammary tumorigenesis in MMTV-HER2/ErbB2 mice (PMID: 23318423)
phenotypes: Tumor incidence reduced to 18% versus 80% in wild-type
Increased tumor latency
Limited effect on metastasis
Reduced number and colony-forming potential of luminal mammary progenitors
Mammosphere morphology and polarity defects
Decreased FAK expression and increased sensitivity to FAK and SRC inhibitors

model_organism.citation: Nedd9 restrains renal cystogenesis in Pkd1-/- mice (PMID: 25139996)
model_organism.knockout_type: full knockout (combined with inducible Pkd1 knockout)
phenotypes: Nedd9 ablation alone did not influence cystogenesis
Strongly enhanced cyst formation in Pkd1-/-;Nedd9-/- mice
Ciliary morphological defects and loss of ciliary adenylate cyclase III
Ciliary resorption defects
Enhanced Src, Erk and S6 activation
Reduced Ca2+ response to stimuli

model_organism.citation: Identification of Nedd9 as a TGF-β-Smad2/3 Target Gene Involved in RANKL-Induced Osteoclastogenesis by Comprehensive Analysis (PMID: 27336669)
phenotypes: Reduced RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis in Nedd9-deficient cells
Partially abrogated stimulatory effect of TGF-β on osteoclastogenesis
No abnormal skeletal phenotype in knockout mice

model_organism.citation: NEDD9 stabilizes focal adhesions, increases binding to the extra-cellular matrix and differentially effects 2D versus 3D cell migration (PMID: 22509381)
model_organism.knockout_type: full knockout (MEFs derived from Nedd9-/- mice)
phenotypes: Increased focal adhesion disassembly rate with increased paxillin phosphorylation
Increased 2D migration but reduced 3D collagen migration
Decreased adhesion to fibronectin
Suppressed β1 integrin activation
Altered myosin light chain kinase activation

model_organism.citation: NEDD9 depletion destabilizes Aurora A kinase and heightens the efficacy of Aurora A inhibitors: implications for treatment of metastatic solid tumors (PMID: 23539442)
model_organism.knockout_type: knockdown (shRNA in xenografts) and knockout cells
phenotypes: Decreased AURKA with increased ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation upon NEDD9 loss
Increased sensitivity to AURKA inhibitors
Combined NEDD9 shRNA and AURKA inhibitor impaired tumor growth and distant metastasis in breast xenografts

model_organism.citation: NEDD9 promotes lung cancer metastasis through epithelial-mesenchymal transition (PMID: 24174333)
model_organism.knockout_type: knockdown (in xenograft) and Nedd9 mouse spontaneous metastasis models
phenotypes: NEDD9 knockdown inhibited migration, invasion and metastasis of lung cancer cells in vitro and in vivo
Reduced EMT and FAK activation

model_organism.citation: Susceptibility-Associated Genetic Variation in NEDD9 Contributes to Prostate Cancer Initiation and Progression (PMID: 33632899)
phenotypes: NEDD9 promoted prostate cancer tumor growth and metastasis in vivo

biological.citation: Unknown et al. 2025 - EIF4A3 Promotes Muscle Atrophy and Aging by Inhibiting the FAK Pathway Through NEDD9 mRNA Destabilization (PMID: 40641186)
biological.summary: NEDD9 mRNA is a direct target of the EJC helicase EIF4A3, which promotes its decay. Loss of NEDD9 reduces FAK and PI3K-Akt signaling and promotes muscle atrophy and aging in myotubes and mice. Pharmacological activation of the NEDD9-FAK pathway abolished the pro-atrophy effects of EIF4A3.
biological.sample_size: n=5 human young/aged; n=6-10 mice per group

biological.citation: Nedd9 restrains renal cystogenesis in Pkd1-/- mice (PMID: 25139996)
biological.summary: Nedd9 expression is deregulated in human ADPKD and a mouse model. Nedd9 loss in Pkd1-/- mice exacerbates cystogenesis, causes ciliary defects and resorption failure through impaired Aurora-A activation, and enhances Src, Erk and S6 signaling. Nedd9 therefore acts as a modifier of ADPKD.

biological.citation: Retinoic acid regulates Schwann cell migration via NEDD9 induction by transcriptional and post-translational mechanisms (PMID: 27085739)
biological.summary: Retinoic acid upregulates NEDD9 in Schwann cells through increased mRNA levels and increased protein stability, and it alters the NEDD9 phospho-isoform ratio. NEDD9 silencing did not affect basal migration but abolished RA-enhanced migration.

biological.citation: NEDD9 links anaplastic thyroid cancer stemness to chromosomal instability through integrated centrosome asymmetry and DNA sensing regulation (PMID: 35449243)
biological.summary: NEDD9 is transcriptionally upregulated and co-expressed with ALDH1A3 in ALDH+ stem-like anaplastic thyroid cancer cells. NEDD9 silencing abolished tolerance of centrosome amplification and micronuclei, including the suppression of STING. It also reduced stemness, CIN and tumor growth in vitro and in vivo, and enhanced paclitaxel effectiveness.

biological.citation: SOX2 promotes hypoxia-induced breast cancer cell migration by inducing NEDD9 expression and subsequent activation of Rac1/HIF-1α signaling (PMID: 31462898)
biological.summary: Hypoxia increases NEDD9 mRNA and protein in breast cancer cells. SOX2 is a positive transcriptional regulator of NEDD9, shown by promoter-luciferase assays and SOX2 knockdown. NEDD9 silencing attenuated hypoxia-induced Rac1 activity and HIF-1α expression, and with them cell migration.

biological.citation: Overexpression of NEDD9 is associated with altered expression of E-Cadherin, β-Catenin and N-Cadherin and predictive of poor prognosis in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 23086683)
biological.summary: NEDD9 was overexpressed in 56.2% of NSCLC samples by IHC relative to normal lung. Overexpression correlated with altered E-cadherin, β-catenin and N-cadherin (EMT markers), lymph node metastasis and shorter overall survival. It was an independent prognostic factor.

biological.citation: NEDD9 sustains hexokinase expression to promote glycolysis (PMID: 35410460)
biological.summary: NEDD9 knockdown impaired glycolysis in lung cancer cells and post-transcriptionally reduced HK1, HK2, PFK1 and GAPDH. These enzymes were also reduced in KP mouse lung tumors with null Nedd9. Hexokinase depletion or 2DG raised NEDD9 expression, suggesting a negative feedback loop.

biological.citation: Baicalein inhibits pancreatic cancer cell proliferation and invasion via suppression of NEDD9 expression and its downstream Akt and ERK signaling pathways (PMID: 28915595)
biological.summary: Baicalein suppressed NEDD9 expression in pancreatic cancer cells, lowering Akt and ERK activity. Akt T308 phosphorylation fell through reduced NEDD9-dependent PDK1 expression. NEDD9 overexpression rescued proliferation and invasion.

biological.citation: SPAG9 regulates HEF1 expression and drives EMT in bladder transitional cell carcinoma via rac1 signaling pathway (PMID: 30662804)
biological.summary: SPAG9 regulates HEF1/NEDD9 expression in bladder cancer cells. SPAG9 overexpression increased migration through HEF1 upregulation and activated Rac1, whereas SPAG9 silencing reduced HEF1 and Rac1 activity. SPAG9 also affected EMT markers (E-cadherin, vimentin).

biological.citation: Glucocorticoid Receptors Drive Breast Cancer Cell Migration and Metabolic Reprogramming via PDK4 (PMID: 37224504)
biological.summary: NEDD9 was identified as a dexamethasone- and pSer134-GR-dependent regulated gene in TNBC cells. It is part of a gene set controlling cell migration alongside CSF1 and RUNX3.
